toegepas.voor: van die eerste klok af tot die laaste een lui
toegepas.na: van die eerste tot die laaste klok
toegepas.rede_vinder: The sentence mixes a prepositional phrase (van ... af) with a clause ending in a verb (tot ... lui); the plain phrase is cleaner and keeps the meaning.
toegepas.fout: Mixes a 'van ... af' phrase with a 'tot ... lui' clause, which reads awkwardly.
toegepas.rede_keurder: The plain phrase from the first to the last bell says the same thing more cleanly.

toegepas.rede_vinder: AWS 2017: comma before 'en' joining two sentences that each have their own subject and verb.
toegepas.fout: Missing AWS comma between two clauses, each with its own subject and verb (Sipho sit / hy praat).
toegepas.rede_keurder: Comma before 'en' joining two full clauses is required by the AWS 2017.

toegepas.rede_vinder: AWS 2017: comma before 'en' joining two sentences that each have their own subject and verb.
toegepas.fout: Missing AWS comma between two full clauses (ouma het siek geword / Naledi het nie gepraat nie).
toegepas.rede_keurder: Comma before 'en' joining two clauses with their own subject and verb.

toegepas.na: Haar keel word warm, en sy
toegepas.rede_vinder: AWS 2017: comma before 'en' joining two sentences that each have their own subject and verb.
toegepas.fout: Missing AWS comma between two full clauses (keel word / sy wil).
toegepas.rede_keurder: Comma before 'en' joining two clauses with their own subject and verb.

toegepas.voor: op die lys en jy kan
toegepas.na: op die lys, en jy kan
toegepas.rede_vinder: AWS 2017: comma before 'en' joining two sentences that each have their own subject and verb, also inside direct speech.
toegepas.fout: Missing AWS comma between two full clauses in direct speech (naam staan / jy kan).
toegepas.rede_keurder: The AWS comma rule applies inside direct speech too.

toegepas.voor: Ruan bly staan en sê sy kry altyd die goeie boeke eerste.
toegepas.na: Ruan bly staan en sê dat sy altyd die goeie boeke eerste kry.
toegepas.rede_vinder: Right after two speech tags 'sê sy', the words 'sê sy kry' first read as 'she says'; 'dat' makes clear that Ruan is speaking about her.
toegepas.fout: Right after the speech tags 'sê sy' and 'voeg sy by', 'sê sy kry' first reads as 'she says', making the reader stumble.
toegepas.rede_keurder: Adding 'dat' removes the misreading without changing who says what.

toegepas.rede_keurder: Comma before 'en' joining two clauses with their own subject and verb.

laat_vaar.voor: Sy ken elke kind se naam en ook die kinders wat nooit boeke uitneem nie.
laat_vaar.na: Sy ken elke kind se naam, ook die name van die kinders wat nooit boeke uitneem nie.
laat_vaar.rede_vinder: As written she knows every name 'and also the children', which joins two unlike objects; the intended point is that she also knows the names of children who never borrow books.
laat_vaar.rede_keurder: The original says she knows the children themselves who never borrow books, not only their names; the proposal narrows that to names, so the meaning moves.

laat_vaar.voor: skuif elke keer die boek oor trekkers nader sonder om te vra
laat_vaar.na: skuif elke keer die boek oor trekkers nader na hom toe sonder om te vra
laat_vaar.rede_vinder: 'nader' does not say closer to whom; 'na hom toe' makes clear the book is moved towards Sipho, which is what the sentence means.
laat_vaar.rede_keurder: 'Nader skuif' is idiomatic and the context already makes clear it moves towards Sipho; the addition only lengthens the sentence.

laat_vaar.voor: Op 'n Dinsdag sit Naledi op die mat met 'n dik boek oor slange.
laat_vaar.na: Op 'n Dinsdag sit Naledi met 'n dik boek oor slange op die mat.
laat_vaar.rede_vinder: In Afrikaans the manner phrase normally comes before the place phrase; the current order reads as if the mat has the book.
laat_vaar.rede_keurder: The original reads naturally, and the proposal creates a worse ambiguity ('slange op die mat' reads as snakes on the mat).

laat_vaar.voor: Sy sit haar stempel neer en sy bly stil
laat_vaar.na: Sy sit haar stempel neer en bly stil
laat_vaar.rede_vinder: The repeated subject 'sy' is unnecessary and makes the sentence wooden; dropping it gives one sentence with two verbs and needs no comma.
laat_vaar.rede_keurder: The repeated 'sy' is normal Afrikaans and part of the story's rhythm; the original does not genuinely jar, so this is a lateral move.

vlae.teks: Juffrou Adonis kyk agter haar tafel op toe Ruan se stem harder word. Sy sit haar stempel neer en sy bly stil waar sy sit. Nou tel sy die stempel weer op en gaan aan met haar werk.
vlae.rede: This paragraph steps back in time inside a present-tense story ('kyk ... op toe ...', then 'Nou'), so the order of events is hard for a Grade 4 reader to follow; fixing it means choosing a tense or moving the paragraph, which is the writer's decision and not a language change.

'Haar keel word warm' is not a usual Afrikaans way of saying someone is getting angry (more usual: 'sy word warm', 'haar wange gloei'); it may be a deliberate bodily sign of anger for this lesson, so it is left unchanged for the writer to decide.
